_comment: Dated inputs to the homeowner payback math. Every value carries the month it was read and a public source URL. The site reads this at build (site/src/data/tariff.ts) and prints the as_of month next to every peso figure, so a stale number is visible rather than silent. Meralco resets the residential rate monthly and posts the advisory around the 10th; refresh this file each month.

electricity_rate.basis: all-in residential rate for a typical household, distribution-utility average
electricity_rate.source_note: GMA News 2026-07-10, reporting the Meralco July 2026 rate advisory. Corroborated by Manila Times 2026-07-11. The August 2026 advisory was not public on 2026-08-09.

install_cost.basis: fully installed grid-tied residential rooftop system, Metro Manila, excluding battery
install_cost.source_note: 2026 installer price guides put a 5 kWp system at PHP 275,000 to 375,000 all-in, which is PHP 55,000 to 75,000 per kWp. The point estimate is the midpoint. Not a quote; a real quote varies with roof access, inverter brand and structural work.

yield.basis: PVGIS SARAH3 Philippine average for a fixed roof-mounted array, 14 percent system loss
yield.source_note: PVGIS v5.3. Per-address yield is fetched live from PVGIS by the roof tool; this constant is the fallback when PVGIS is unreachable.

net_metering.source_note: DOE circular effective 2026-04-01 cut the distribution-utility decision window from 20 to 10 working days. The residential capacity cap stays at 100 kW. Vendor guides report a non-residential lift from 100 kW to 1 MW under the same circular; no primary DOE text confirms it, so that figure is not published on the site.
